items.t: MHRA advice for all topical steroids (not a product label): long-term use (generally 6 months or more) of moderate or stronger topical steroids, particularly for eczema, can cause topical steroid withdrawal reactions (intense redness, stinging and burning spreading beyond the treated area). Use the lowest effective potency.

src.q: adverse reactions have been reported following long-term (generally 6 months or more) use of moderate or stronger potency topical steroids, particularly when used for eczema treatment
The lowest potency topical steroid for effective treatment should be used

items.t: MHRA advice for all miconazole products (not a product label): miconazole, including topical forms, can enhance the effect of warfarin; monitor the anticoagulant effect and reduce the warfarin dose if needed.

src.q: if miconazole and warfarin are used concurrently, the anticoagulant effect should be carefully monitored and, if necessary, the dose of warfarin reduced

items.t: BUMPS (topical corticosteroids, mometasone named; not a product label): topical corticosteroids can be used in pregnancy. Miconazole is not covered by this leaflet.

src.q: Topical corticosteroids can be used in pregnancy.

items.t: SPS (mometasone; not a product label): mometasone applied to the skin can be used during breastfeeding (high potency). Miconazole is not covered by this page.

src.q: When applied to the skin, inhaled or used intranasally, mometasone can be used during breastfeeding.
Mometasone is considered high potency when applied as a cream or ointment.
